summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout data with 98.7 percent CGM coverage at a 5-minute cadence show an average glucose of 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0 percent, time above range 8.9 percent, time below range 5.1 percent, and a coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent. Overall control is good, and the 04:00 to 09:00 local window is close to ideal. Two patterns stand out: a hypoglycemia cluster at 18:00 to 19:00 local (time below range 7.7 and 15.3 percent, with 41 and 42 mg/dL nadirs) and a second cluster at 23:00 to 03:00 local (10 to 18.5 percent), plus a sustained afternoon plateau peaking at 16:00 local (average 162.8 mg/dL, time above range 32.1 percent). No carbohydrate entries exist in the entire period (0 carb entries, 0 grams, no extended carbs), so all meal coverage runs through UAM with COB reported as 0 in all sampled loop statuses. Loop statuses show effective sensitivity between 27.8 and 124.0 mg/dL per unit against a flat profile ISF of 56, insulin on board reaching 4.73 and 5.935 units against roughly 16 to 20 units per day, and effective loop targets between 80 and 116 mg/dL that do not match the declared 90 and 100 mg/dL schedule. The evidence points to unannounced carbohydrate plus aggressive high-glucose correction as the shared driver of both the afternoon highs and the evening lows, rather than to a defective basal profile.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is 98.7 percent with 3995 valid entries against 4046 expected, 5-minute cadence, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 minutes, zero invalid, duplicate, or out-of-period entries. Local timezone is BST at UTC plus 60 minutes and hourly_glucose_local maps consistently as hourly_glucose shifted by one hour, so local-hour analysis is reliable. All 17 profile decision_inventory items are present with values, and all 6 AAPS groups are present with non-null components. The profile ISF is a single flat segment of 56 mg/dL per unit, consistent with the profile name recorded in the events. Scheduled basal sums to 16.2 units per day, matching the profile label. Carbohydrate telemetry is entirely absent: carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0, carb_treatment_entries empty, extended_carb_entries 0. Only representative subsets were supplied (40 of 2315 treatments, 24 of 6214 device statuses), which supports pattern-level but not event-level conclusions. The 2026-08-07 daily row contains only 33 readings and is a partial day.

analysis_steps.findings: Aggregate time below range is 5.1 percent, above the commonly used 4 percent guideline, and it is concentrated rather than diffuse. By local hour, time below range is 18.5 percent at 01:00, 15.3 percent at 19:00, 11.4 percent at 00:00, 10.2 percent at 03:00, 10.1 percent at 02:00 and 23:00, and 7.7 percent at 18:00, while 08:00 to 17:00 stays at or below 2 percent apart from 4.7 percent at 13:00. Three level-2 episodes appear in glucose_extremes: 42 mg/dL on 2026-08-13 at 18:00 to 18:15 local, 41 mg/dL on 2026-08-14 at 19:04 to 19:14 local, and 42 mg/dL on 2026-08-21 at 07:19 local. Two of three fall inside the evening hypoglycemia window. Severe hyperglycemia is limited to two isolated excursions near 290 mg/dL on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18. Worst days are 2026-08-14 (time in range 70.8 percent) and 2026-08-18 (time in range 71.9 percent, time below range 12.8 percent). Documented confounders inside the window are GLP-1 1.25 mg on 08-14, 08-17, and 08-20, a profile switch on 08-13, site changes on 08-10, 08-13, and 08-17, sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21, and occlusion plus pump-error announcements on 08-19 shortly before that day's 264 mg/dL peak. Response windows show large post-correction undershoots: 234 to 56 mg/dL in 120 minutes on 08-14, 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes on 08-19, and 174 to 66 mg/dL in 120 minutes on 08-15.

analysis_steps.findings: The profile basal schedule is 0.6 U/h at 00:00, 0.7 at 05:00, 0.8 at 06:00, 0.7 at 10:00, 0.5 at 16:00, 0.6 at 18:00, and 0.7 at 19:00, with targets 90 mg/dL at 00:00, 100 at 08:00, and 90 at 23:00. The 04:00 to 09:00 local window shows time in range 95 to 99 percent with time below range of 1.3 to 4.8 percent, indicating the overnight and dawn segments are broadly well matched. Two apparent mismatches exist: the lowest basal segment (0.5 U/h from 16:00) coincides with the highest hourly average (162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 local, time above range 32.1 percent), and the basal step up to 0.7 U/h at 19:00 coincides with the highest daytime time below range (15.3 percent at 19:00 local). Neither mismatch can currently be attributed to basal. Both documented evening level-2 events follow large afternoon correction and UAM activity two to six hours earlier, and with a 10-hour DIA that insulin remains nominally active. The afternoon plateau coincides with completely unannounced intake, with loop statuses reporting COB 0 alongside positive deviations of 2.3 to 7.1 and insulin requirements of 0.77 to 2.59 units, which is the signature of unannounced meals rather than a fasting basal deficit. Basal, CR, and safety multipliers are corroborated as live: the logged maxSafeBasal of 4 U/h on 2026-08-14 at 19:40 local matches exactly the derived minimum of max_basal 12, 6.0 times the 0.7 U/h basal, and 5.0 times the 0.8 U/h maximum basal. Targets do not reconcile: sampled loop target_bg values include 80, 84, 86, 87, 90, 96.4, 97, 99, 100, 101, 104, 105, 106, 108, and 116 mg/dL, which the declared schedule and the logged temporary targets do not explain, and which autosens target modulation cannot explain because both autosens target switches are false.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratios of 13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5, and 12.6 g/U cannot be evaluated because there were zero carbohydrate entries in 14 days, so no meal bolus was ever driven by a carb ratio. The same CR values appear in loop reason strings by time of day, confirming the profile is live and that CR still feeds the dynamic sensitivity computation, but its correctness is untestable from these data. The flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit is not the operative sensitivity because dynamic sensitivity is enabled with a 70 percent adjustment factor and autosens is disabled. Observed variable sensitivity spans 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit, weaker than profile at low glucose and low insulin on board (108.4, 111.9, 114.6, 124.0) and roughly twice as strong as profile at high glucose with high insulin on board (27.8 at 245.7 mg/dL with 5.935 units on board, 37.9 at 262.2 mg/dL with 4.73 units on board). This asymmetry matches the observed pattern of a persistent 130 to 160 mg/dL plateau followed by large overshoots after high-glucose corrections. DIA of 10 hours with a free-peak insulin model flattens insulin decay and keeps afternoon insulin nominally active into the evening hypoglycemia window and evening insulin into the overnight window, but DIA cannot be validated directly because no clean fasting single-bolus decay curve exists in the supplied response windows. Correction sizes are mostly 0.05 to 0.35 units, so most glucose movement in the response windows is not bolus-driven.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled and are the only meal coverage present, since carbohydrate entries are zero and all sampled statuses report COB 0. Aggregate outcomes remain good, so disabling either is unsupported. Among activation conditions, smb_always_enabled true makes smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false functionally inert, and doubly inert because no carbohydrates are entered; there is no internal contradiction. One material interaction exists: with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false, a high temporary target suppresses SMB despite smb_always_enabled being true. Temporary targets of 135 mg/dL were set for 180 minutes on 2026-08-17 at 13:30 to 16:30 local and for 180 minutes on 2026-08-18 at 15:24 to 18:24 local, both inside the afternoon plateau, and on 08-17 a 0.15 unit correction at 126 mg/dL was followed by 190 mg/dL at 180 minutes. Total high-target exposure is roughly 435 minutes out of 336 hours, so this explains part of the plateau on those specific days only, not the 14-day pattern. On SMB strength and frequency, the 3-minute interval against a 5-minute CGM cadence permits an SMB on essentially every loop cycle, which combined with a 10-hour DIA is the mechanistic path to the observed insulin on board of 4.73 and 5.935 units on a 16 to 20 unit per day scale. A separate consistency finding is that the configured max_uam_smb_basal_minutes of 20 implies a UAM SMB ceiling of roughly 0.17 to 0.27 units at the profile basal rates, yet reason strings record microbolusing of 0.4 units, SMB values of 0.3 units, and one UAM high boost SMB of 1.6 units, so the delivered SMB size is being governed by boost logic rather than by the declared minute caps.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens disabled together with dynamic sensitivity enabled is a standard, non-contradictory combination, and both autosens target switches being false is consistent with autosens being off. Observed sensitivity_ratio values of 1.0, 0.98, 0.94, 0.92, 0.91, 0.88, and 0.79 are treated as neutral or restraining current adjustments, not as evidence about the autosens switch; the 0.79 value on 2026-08-16 accompanied a 120-minute zero temporary basal, showing the sensitivity layer does restrain dosing at times. The 70 percent dynamic ISF factor produces a very wide effective sensitivity swing around the flat 56 mg/dL per unit anchor, from about 124 at 69.8 mg/dL with negative insulin on board to 27.8 at 245.7 mg/dL with 5.935 units on board. This reproduces the observed asymmetry of relatively weak correction across the 130 to 160 mg/dL plateau and roughly double-strength dosing above 200 mg/dL, followed by 41 to 56 mg/dL nadirs. On safety limits, max_basal of 12 U/h is non-binding because the effective ceiling is the derived maxSafeBasal of 3.0 to 4.2 U/h, confirmed twice in the logs, so changing it would not alter delivery. By contrast max_iob of 25 units exceeds the entire estimated daily insulin requirement of roughly 16 to 20 units and is about four times the highest insulin on board actually observed at 5.935 units, so it provides no practical ceiling in a system that has already produced 41 to 56 mg/dL nadirs after stacking. The final status in the package on 2026-08-21 at 22:09 local shows 245.7 mg/dL, 5.935 units on board, an effective target of 80 mg/dL, sensitivity 27.8, an insulin requirement of 2.12 units, and a 4 U/h rate, with no subsequent CGM data available; a sensor change earlier that day is an unresolved alternative explanation for that trace. The carbohydrate absorption group governed nothing during the period because COB was zero in all sampled statuses, so both of its values are unvalidated rather than validated. Overall, the automation is compensating for a data-entry gap rather than for a defective basal profile, with DIA of 10 hours and the flat ISF acting as amplifiers.

analysis_steps.findings: The user-declared aaps_profile.analysis_context has source declared_by_user and declared_at 2026-08-21, with meal_strategies as an empty array, period_exceptions null, and strategy_stable_for_period null. There is therefore no declared prebolus_minutes, immediate_bolus_percent, or e-carb field in the package, and no representative-period rule can be applied. The only percentage present is bolus_wizard_percentage of 100 percent, which scales bolus-wizard output and is not an immediate-bolus split. Observed execution is a carb-free, correction-and-UAM-only regimen across 655 insulin entries and 275.95 units, with no meal bolus, bolus wizard, or carbohydrate event in any supplied treatment record. Declared context and observed telemetry therefore agree that no meal-bolus workflow is in use. Three recurring rises exist despite zero carbohydrate records: a morning rise from 110.5 to 148.0 mg/dL between 08:00 and 10:00 local with zero to 1.2 percent time below range, a midday to afternoon complex peaking at 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 local, and a late-evening rise reaching maxima of 204, 234, and 249 mg/dL between 20:00 and 23:00 local that runs into the overnight hypoglycemia cluster. Corrections are placed into already-rising or already-high glucose rather than ahead of intake, and 17 of 24 response windows involve doses of 0.25 units or less. Four windows show a hypoglycemic nadir followed within 60 to 120 minutes by a rise too large and fast for basal withdrawal alone: 71 to 225 mg/dL on 08-12, 47 to 204 on 08-13, 56 to 136 on 08-14, and 53 to 158 on 08-16, which is consistent with unlogged rescue carbohydrate. This closes a plausible loop in which unannounced intake drives boosted UAM dosing, insulin accumulates under a long DIA with no effective insulin-on-board ceiling, glucose overshoots downward in the evening, unlogged rescue carbohydrate follows, and the loop then sees a fresh unannounced rise.

analysis_steps.findings: Extended carbohydrates were not used at any point: extended_carb_entries is 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min is null, carb_treatment_entries is an empty array, and all 24 response windows report is_extended_carbs false. No e-carb amount, start offset, duration, or observed action time exists to assess, and no duration is inferred from any aggregate. The absorption parameters min_5m_carbimpact of 8 mg/dL per 5 minutes and meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 governed nothing during the period because COB was zero in all sampled statuses. E-carbs are not equated with a pump extended bolus; e-carbs declare carbohydrate arriving over time so the algorithm can build COB, whereas an extended bolus delivers insulin over time, and neither appears in the package. Indirect evidence of prolonged rises exists, for example the 2026-08-14 window rising 135 mg/dL at 240 minutes and remaining 131 mg/dL above start at 360 minutes, and the afternoon plateau failing to return to baseline, but slow absorption is only one candidate explanation alongside sequential unannounced eating, GLP-1 dosing on 08-14, 08-17, and 08-20 altering gastric emptying, SMB suppression under the 180-minute high temporary targets on 08-17 and 08-18, and the 08-19 occlusion. Because those effects are not separable in the supplied data, no e-carb inference is drawn.

analysis_steps.findings: A contradiction audit against aaps_profile, profile_context, and decision_inventory confirms all 17 profile values and all 6 AAPS groups with 19 non-null components, so no AAPS group qualifies for a verify decision. Two earlier working hypotheses are corrected. First, the idea that the 16:00 basal segment of 0.5 U/h is too low is retired as a standalone explanation, because the afternoon peak coincides with unannounced intake, with SMB gated off by 180-minute high temporary targets on two of the worst afternoons, and because adding afternoon insulin would feed the 18:00 to 19:00 hypoglycemia cluster under a 10-hour DIA. Second, the idea that overnight basal or the 90 mg/dL overnight target is the primary cause of overnight lows is downgraded, because effective loop targets range from 80 to 116 mg/dL and do not track the declared schedule, so a declared-target change would have uncertain effect. Competing explanations that remain unseparated are overnight basal excess, the long DIA tail combined with evening stacking, and the overnight target. The one mechanism supported by convergent evidence across all stages is that unannounced carbohydrate forces UAM to chase rises with dynamic-sensitivity-boosted microboluses at a 3-minute interval, insulin accumulates under a 10-hour DIA, and the max_iob limit of 25 units provides no practical ceiling at an estimated 16 to 20 units per day. The safest first action is therefore the one guard that reduces worst-case exposure without altering dose calculation, followed sequentially by the sensitivity factor, then SMB frequency, then carbohydrate logging. Profile parameters are kept because basal is corroborated in the 04:00 to 09:00 window, ISF is only an anchor for a dynamic calculation, CR is untestable, DIA cannot be validated without a clean fasting decay curve, and targets are not reliably reflected in loop behavior.

strengths: CGM data quality is excellent: 98.7 percent coverage, 5-minute cadence, 3995 valid entries with zero invalid, duplicate, or out-of-period records, and a largest gap of only 65 minutes, so pattern analysis rests on solid data.

Overall glycemic outcomes are good for a fully unannounced-carbohydrate regimen: average 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0 percent, and a coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent, which sits within the commonly used stability marker of 36 percent.

The overnight into dawn window from 04:00 to 09:00 local is close to ideal, with time in range of 95.2, 97.5, 98.7, 98.2, and 91.1 percent and time below range of 4.8 percent or less, indicating the 0.6 to 0.8 U/h basal segments covering that period are broadly well matched.
Severe hyperglycemia is rare and episodic rather than habitual: only two excursions near 290 mg/dL in 14 days, on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18, with no sustained very high periods.

The profile is complete and internally consistent, and the logged maxSafeBasal of 4 U/h reconciles exactly with the declared basal rate and the configured safety multipliers, confirming the declared configuration was live during the period.

Automated safety behavior is present and functional: loop statuses show zero temporary basals and 120-minute suspensions when low predictions appear, and sensitivity ratios below 1 show the sensitivity layer restraining dosing at times.

Event annotation quality is good for non-carbohydrate items, with site changes, sensor changes, GLP-1 doses, occlusion, pump error, and profile switches all recorded, which allowed several confounders to be identified and excluded from attribution.

issues.title: Time below range of 5.1 percent concentrated in two clock windows
issues.detail: Aggregate time below range exceeds the commonly used 4 percent guideline and is concentrated at 18:00 to 19:00 local (7.7 and 15.3 percent) and 23:00 to 03:00 local (10.1 to 18.5 percent), with three level-2 episodes at 41, 42, and 42 mg/dL. Two of the three follow large afternoon correction and UAM activity two to six hours earlier.

issues.title: Insulin accumulation without a practical insulin-on-board ceiling
issues.detail: Insulin on board reached 4.73 units on 2026-08-19 and 5.935 units on 2026-08-21 against an estimated 16 to 20 units per day, while max_iob is set to 25 units, roughly four times the highest value observed and above the entire daily requirement, so the limit never constrains dosing.

issues.title: Wide effective sensitivity swing around the flat profile anchor
issues.detail: With dynamic sensitivity enabled at a 70 percent factor and a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit, observed effective sensitivity ranges from 124.0 at low glucose to 27.8 at 245.7 mg/dL, which corresponds to weak correction across the 130 to 160 mg/dL plateau and roughly double-strength dosing above 200 mg/dL, followed by 41 to 56 mg/dL nadirs.

issues.title: SMB permitted on essentially every loop cycle
issues.detail: An SMB interval of 3 minutes against a 5-minute CGM cadence allows a microbolus on nearly every cycle, which combined with a 10-hour DIA is the mechanistic route to the observed insulin accumulation and post-correction overshoots of minus 168 and minus 178 mg/dL in 120 minutes.

issues.title: No carbohydrate information anywhere in the period
issues.detail: Zero carbohydrate entries, zero grams, no extended carbohydrates, and COB reported as 0 in all sampled loop statuses mean every meal is handled reactively by UAM, and carb ratio, absorption settings, prebolus timing, and any bolus split remain untestable.

issues.title: Effective loop targets do not match the declared target schedule
issues.detail: Declared targets are 90, 100, and 90 mg/dL, but sampled loop target_bg values span 80 to 116 mg/dL, dropping toward 80 when glucose is high and rising toward 116 when low predictions appear. Autosens target modulation is disabled, and logged temporary targets explain at most one value, so the discrepancy is unexplained and reduces confidence in any target change.

issues.title: High temporary targets suppressed SMB during two of the worst afternoons
issues.detail: With smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false, the 180-minute temporary targets of 135 mg/dL on 2026-08-17 at 13:30 to 16:30 local and 2026-08-18 at 15:24 to 18:24 local gated SMB off inside the afternoon plateau, which explains part of the elevation on those specific days but not the 14-day pattern.

issues.title: Probable unlogged rescue carbohydrate after hypoglycemia
issues.detail: Four windows show a nadir followed within 60 to 120 minutes by a rise too large for basal withdrawal alone, including 47 to 204 mg/dL on 2026-08-13 and 71 to 225 mg/dL on 2026-08-12, which suggests hypoglycemia depth and true meal load are both under-represented in the data.

recommendations.title: Discuss lowering the maximum insulin-on-board limit toward observed usage
recommendations.description: The max_iob value of 25 units exceeds the entire estimated daily insulin requirement of roughly 16 to 20 units and is about four times the highest insulin on board actually observed in the period, 5.935 units on 2026-08-21. It therefore provides no practical ceiling in a system that reached 41 to 56 mg/dL nadirs after documented stacking episodes on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, and 2026-08-19. This is a guard rather than a dose-calculation parameter, so it is the least entangled item in the whole package: it does not alter carb ratio, sensitivity, basal, or SMB sizing, and it only limits worst-case accumulation. Any candidate value should still sit clearly above normal peak usage so that routine dosing is unaffected, and should be discussed with the care team before any change.

suggested_change.observe: Whether any loop status reports the insulin-on-board limit being reached during normal meals, and whether the 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 03:00 time below range values fall.

recommendations.title: Discuss a more conservative dynamic sensitivity factor as the second step
recommendations.description: Observed effective sensitivity of 27.8 mg/dL per unit at 245.7 mg/dL is roughly twice as aggressive as the flat profile anchor of 56, while values of 108 to 124 at low glucose are roughly twice as weak. This asymmetry matches both the persistent afternoon plateau and the large downward overshoots of minus 168 and minus 178 mg/dL in 120 minutes. Reducing the adjustment factor narrows that swing without touching basal, carb ratio, or SMB frequency. This must be tested separately from any SMB interval change, because both explain the same overshoot evidence and changing them together would make the result uninterpretable.

suggested_change.observe: Effective variable sensitivity values above 200 mg/dL and the size of post-correction drops at 120 minutes.

recommendations.title: Consider a longer SMB interval only after the sensitivity step is evaluated
recommendations.description: A 3-minute SMB interval against a 5-minute CGM cadence permits a microbolus on essentially every loop cycle, which under a 10-hour DIA is a direct contributor to accumulation. Note that the declared minute caps do not appear to bound delivered SMB size in this build, since reason strings record microboluses of 0.4 units and one boosted SMB of 1.6 units against a cap that implies roughly 0.17 to 0.27 units, so interval is the more reliable lever in this group. This step is listed only to fix the safe order; it should not be attempted until the sensitivity change has been observed.

suggested_change.observe: Peak insulin on board per day and whether afternoon time above range worsens.

recommendations.title: Begin logging carbohydrate for one meal, including rescue carbohydrate
recommendations.description: Zero carbohydrate entries in 14 days is the single reason carb ratio, absorption settings, prebolus timing, and any bolus split remain untestable, and it is also why UAM must chase every rise reactively. Logging grams and time for the morning meal only, plus every rescue carbohydrate at any hour, changes no insulin-delivery setting yet unblocks the largest number of downstream questions. The morning window is proposed because it carries the lowest hypoglycemia exposure of any meal window at 0 to 1.2 percent time below range.

suggested_change.action: Log carbohydrate grams and timestamps for the 08:00 to 10:00 local meal and for all rescue carbohydrate, for 10 consecutive days, with no other change.
suggested_change.observe: Whether COB becomes non-zero in loop statuses, whether morning time above range at 10:00 local falls, and how often rescue carbohydrate is actually taken.

recommendations.title: Review the interaction between high temporary targets and SMB suppression
recommendations.description: Because smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled is false, the 180-minute temporary targets of 135 mg/dL used on 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18 suppressed SMB inside the afternoon plateau even though smb_always_enabled is true. This is a settings interaction worth understanding rather than an error, and it affects how those two days should be interpreted. No change to the switch is proposed, because enabling SMB under high temporary targets would remove a deliberate brake in a system already prone to stacking.

suggested_change.action: Keep the current value and note that long high temporary targets will continue to suppress SMB; consider using shorter durations if the intent was only brief protection.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all 17 profile values unchanged for now, including the 16:00 basal segment of 0.5 U/h and the 19:00 segment of 0.7 U/h, and verify overnight basal specifically by comparing 23:00 to 03:00 local glucose on nights that followed a quiet evening against nights that followed an evening excursion above 200 mg/dL.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The apparent profile mismatches do not survive separation of effects. The 04:00 to 09:00 local window shows 95 to 99 percent time in range on the existing 0.6 to 0.8 U/h segments, which corroborates the basal level. The afternoon peak at 16:00 local coincides with completely unannounced carbohydrate, with COB reported as 0 alongside deviations of 2.3 to 7.1, and with SMB gated off by 180-minute high temporary targets on two of the worst afternoons, so it is not established as a basal deficit; raising basal there would also push insulin into the 18:00 to 19:00 hypoglycemia window under a 10-hour DIA. The evening hypoglycemia cluster follows documented large afternoon corrections rather than tracking the basal schedule. Targets cannot be changed with confidence because effective loop targets span 80 to 116 mg/dL and do not follow the declared 90 and 100 mg/dL schedule. Carb ratio is untestable with zero carbohydrate entries, DIA cannot be validated without a clean fasting single-bolus decay curve, and the flat ISF of 56 is only an anchor for a dynamic calculation whose factor is the more direct lever. The automation guard and sensitivity factor therefore carry a stronger evidence base than any profile row.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Over the next 10 days, stratify the 23:00 to 03:00 local glucose curves by whether the preceding 20:00 to 23:00 window exceeded 200 mg/dL. If lows occur on quiet evenings too, overnight basal or the overnight target becomes the supported target for a single small change; if lows occur only after evening excursions, the cause is the insulin tail and no basal change is indicated.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: time below range at 00:00 local is 11.4 percent and at 01:00 local is 18.5 percent, which is the highest of any hour, but the 04:00 to 07:00 local window on the adjacent 0.6 and 0.7 U/h segments shows 95 to 99 percent time in range. Uncertainty: the overnight lows follow evening excursions reaching 204, 234, and 249 mg/dL and a 10-hour DIA keeps evening insulin active, so an insulin tail is at least as plausible as basal excess. Dependencies: cannot be separated from the SMB frequency and dynamic sensitivity changes proposed ahead of it, and the effective overnight target is uncertain because loop targets ranged from 80 to 116 mg/dL. Withholding change until the night-stratification check is complete.

Evidence: the 05:00 local hour shows 95.2 percent time in range, 4.8 percent time below range, and no time above range, and the 06:00 and 07:00 hours are similarly strong. Uncertainty: minimal for this segment; the single 42 mg/dL reading at 07:19 local on 2026-08-21 occurred on the day of a sensor change and is excluded from attribution. Dependencies: none that would justify a change; this segment is one of the best-performing parts of the profile.

Evidence: the 06:00 to 09:00 local hours show time in range of 97.5, 98.7, 98.2, and 91.1 percent with time below range of 2.5 percent or less, indicating the dawn step is well matched. Uncertainty: the rise beginning at 08:00 local reaches 148.0 mg/dL by 10:00 with 20.2 percent time above range, but with zero carbohydrate entries this is most consistent with an unannounced morning meal rather than a dawn basal deficit. Dependencies: resolution requires the morning carbohydrate logging observation before any basal change here could be justified.

Evidence: hours 10:00 to 15:00 local average 148.0, 132.3, 141.3, 135.0, 148.1, and 153.0 mg/dL with time above range of 7.5 to 26.3 percent. Uncertainty: high. Loop statuses across this window report COB 0 with deviations of 2.3 to 7.1 and insulin requirements up to 2.59 units, the signature of unannounced intake rather than a fasting basal shortfall, and no fasting window exists in the data to test the segment. Dependencies: any upward change here would add insulin that remains active into the 18:00 to 19:00 hypoglycemia cluster under a 10-hour DIA, so it must wait until that cluster is resolved.

Evidence: the 16:00 local hour has the highest average of the day at 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent time above range and 0.0 percent time below range, and it carries the lowest basal rate in the profile, which superficially suggests underdosing. Uncertainty: high, and the earlier working hypothesis of a basal deficit here is explicitly retired. Two of the worst afternoons, 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18, had 180-minute temporary targets of 135 mg/dL that suppressed SMB entirely because smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled is false, and all afternoon rises are unannounced. Dependencies: raising this segment would feed the 18:00 to 19:00 window where time below range is 7.7 and 15.3 percent with 41 and 42 mg/dL nadirs, so change is unsafe before the automation steps and carbohydrate logging are evaluated.

Evidence: the 18:00 local hour shows 7.7 percent time below range with a minimum of 42 mg/dL, and the 2026-08-13 level-2 episode falls in this hour. Uncertainty: high as to cause. That episode followed a 0.2 unit correction at 172 mg/dL roughly five hours earlier and a documented afternoon UAM sequence, so the insulin tail under a 10-hour DIA is the leading explanation rather than the basal rate itself. Dependencies: the max_iob, dynamic sensitivity, and SMB interval steps all reduce the same tail; changing basal at the same time would make attribution impossible.

Evidence: the 19:00 local hour has the highest daytime time below range at 15.3 percent with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, and the basal schedule steps up into this hour, which appears counterintuitive. Uncertainty: high. The 2026-08-14 level-2 episode in this hour followed a 0.2 unit correction at 234 mg/dL plus a 1.1 unit bolus about two to three hours earlier, and the loop enacted 3.6 U/h at 19:40 local, so delivered insulin dominates the scheduled basal contribution here. Dependencies: this hour is the primary readout for the max_iob and dynamic sensitivity steps, so it must be observed unchanged while those are tested.

Evidence: carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, and carb_treatment_entries is empty for the full 14 days, so this ratio never drove a meal bolus. Uncertainty: complete for meal dosing; the value is not validated, only untested. Dependencies: it still feeds the dynamic sensitivity computation, since carb ratio values appear in loop reason strings, so it is not inert, but any change would alter that computation without a single meal outcome to justify it. Change withheld until carbohydrate logging produces evidence.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entries exist in the period, and the 04:00 to 08:00 local window shows 95.2 to 98.7 percent time in range with no meal signature. Uncertainty: complete; the ratio is untestable. Dependencies: the value appears in loop reason strings and therefore scales dynamic sensitivity, so changing it blindly would confound the sensitivity step that is already proposed. Keep.

Evidence: a consistent morning rise from 110.5 to 148.0 mg/dL exists between 08:00 and 10:00 local, but with zero carbohydrate entries no bolus was ever calculated from this ratio. Uncertainty: complete for validation purposes. Dependencies: this is the specific ratio that the proposed morning carbohydrate logging observation would first make testable, so change is deliberately deferred to after that observation rather than guessed now.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entries exist, so this ratio has not been exercised for meal dosing. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: this ratio applies to the 16:00 to 20:00 local window that contains both the day's highest average glucose and, from 18:00, the day's worst hypoglycemia exposure; any change here would act on both problems simultaneously in opposite directions and cannot be evaluated. Keep.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entries exist, despite a clear recurring evening rise reaching 204, 234, and 249 mg/dL between 20:00 and 23:00 local. Uncertainty: complete for validation. Dependencies: this window feeds directly into the 23:00 to 03:00 hypoglycemia cluster, so it is the least safe place to introduce additional meal insulin before the overnight cause is separated. Keep.

Evidence: dynamic sensitivity is enabled with a 70 percent adjustment factor and autosens is disabled, and observed effective sensitivity ranges from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit, so the flat 56 value is an anchor rather than the operative sensitivity. Uncertainty: the asymmetric dosing behavior is real and well evidenced, but it is produced by the scaling factor around this anchor, not by the anchor alone. Dependencies: changing the anchor and the dynamic factor together would violate the one-change-at-a-time rule and would make the result uninterpretable, so the factor is proposed as the single lever and the anchor is kept unchanged.

Evidence: overnight time below range is 11.4 percent at 00:00 and 18.5 percent at 01:00 local, which would normally support raising an overnight target. Uncertainty: high, because sampled loop target_bg values span 80 to 116 mg/dL and do not follow the declared schedule, autosens target modulation is disabled, and logged temporary targets explain at most one value, so a declared-target change may not produce the expected effect. Dependencies: the night-stratification check must first establish whether the lows are target-driven or an evening insulin tail. Keep pending that check.

Evidence: the daytime window covered by this target shows 0 to 1.8 percent time below range from 08:00 to 12:00 local and no hypoglycemia pressure, while the afternoon elevation is attributable to unannounced carbohydrate. Uncertainty: the effective loop target in this window was observed as low as 80 mg/dL, which is unexplained and is itself a contributor to correction aggression at high glucose. Dependencies: the target discrepancy is not represented in decision_inventory and cannot be resolved by changing the declared value; keep and observe.

Evidence: the 23:00 local hour shows 10.1 percent time below range and an average of 105.7 mg/dL while descending from the evening rise. Uncertainty: high, for the same reason as the 00:00 target: effective loop targets do not track the declared schedule, so the causal link between this declared value and the observed lows is not established. Dependencies: this segment shares its cause with the 00:00 target and the evening insulin tail, and only one of the three can be changed at a time. Keep pending the night-stratification check.

Evidence: DIA of 10 hours with a free-peak insulin model flattens decay and is mechanistically implicated in carrying afternoon insulin into the 18:00 to 19:00 hypoglycemia cluster and evening insulin into the overnight cluster, alongside observed insulin on board of 4.73 and 5.935 units. Uncertainty: high, because DIA cannot be validated without a clean fasting decay curve after a single bolus with no subsequent intake, and no such window exists in the supplied response windows, which are all non-monotonic and imply unlogged food. Dependencies: shortening DIA would change insulin-on-board accounting across every other proposed step simultaneously, which is exactly the dependent-change pattern to avoid. Keep, and reconsider only if the max_iob and sensitivity steps fail to reduce the evening lows.

Evidence: with zero carbohydrate entries and COB reported as 0 in all 24 sampled loop statuses, UAM is the only mechanism providing meal coverage, and aggregate outcomes remain good at 86.0 percent time in range and 32.6 percent coefficient of variation. Uncertainty: the identified problem is the magnitude and timing of UAM dosing, not its existence. Dependencies: disabling either switch would remove all meal coverage and would very likely worsen the afternoon and evening hyperglycemia; the appropriate levers are the sensitivity factor and the SMB interval. Both components have values, so verify does not apply.

Evidence: smb_always_enabled true makes the COB-related switches functionally inert, and they are doubly inert because no carbohydrates were entered; there is no internal contradiction in the group. The high-temporary-target gate did suppress SMB during 180-minute targets of 135 mg/dL on 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18, accounting for roughly 435 minutes out of 336 hours. Uncertainty: that exposure explains part of the elevation on those two days but not the 14-day afternoon pattern. Dependencies: enabling SMB under high temporary targets would remove a deliberate brake in a system already showing insulin accumulation to 5.935 units, so change is unsupported. All five components have values, so verify does not apply.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=5 to 8 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: a 3-minute interval against a 5-minute CGM cadence permits a microbolus on essentially every loop cycle, and observed insulin on board reached 4.73 units on 2026-08-19 and 5.935 units on 2026-08-21 against roughly 16 to 20 units per day, with post-correction drops of minus 168 and minus 178 mg/dL in 120 minutes. Uncertainty: medium. The same overshoots are equally consistent with the 27.8 to 43 mg/dL per unit effective sensitivity at high glucose, so frequency and per-dose strength are not yet separated; in addition the declared minute caps do not appear to bound delivered SMB size in this build, since reason strings record 0.4 unit microboluses and one 1.6 unit boosted SMB against a cap implying roughly 0.17 to 0.27 units, which is why only the interval component is proposed for change and the two minute caps are left as they are. Dependencies: this must be tested strictly after and separately from the dynamic sensitivity change and the max_iob change; changing it in parallel would make the result uninterpretable. All three components have values, so verify does not apply.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: max_iob of 25 units exceeds the entire estimated daily insulin requirement of roughly 16 to 20 units and is about four times the highest insulin on board observed, 5.935 units on 2026-08-21 at 245.7 mg/dL with an effective target of 80 and sensitivity of 27.8; no sequence of dosing in this dataset could ever have reached the limit, so it provides no practical ceiling in a system that produced 41 to 56 mg/dL nadirs. The max_basal component is left unchanged because the effective ceiling is the derived maxSafeBasal of 3.0 to 4.2 U/h, confirmed twice in the logs, so 12 U/h is already non-binding and lowering it would not change delivery. Uncertainty: low for the direction, moderate for the exact value, since true total daily dose is unknown because delivered basal is not summed anywhere in the package; the candidate range is therefore deliberately set well above observed peak usage. Dependencies: this is a guard rather than a dose-calculation input, so it is the least entangled change and is sequenced first, before the sensitivity and SMB interval steps. Both components have values, so verify does not apply.

parameter_decisions.suggested_value: autosens_enabled=false; dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true; autosens_raises_target=false; autosens_lowers_target=false; dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=55 to 60 %
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: the four switches are internally consistent, since dynamic sensitivity supersedes autosens and both autosens target switches correctly follow autosens being disabled, so none of them is proposed for change. The adjustment factor of 70 percent, however, produces effective sensitivity from 124.0 mg/dL per unit at 69.8 mg/dL with negative insulin on board down to 27.8 at 245.7 mg/dL with 5.935 units on board, roughly a two-fold swing in each direction around the flat 56 anchor, which matches the observed pattern of weak correction across the 130 to 160 mg/dL plateau and roughly double-strength dosing above 200 mg/dL followed by 41 to 56 mg/dL nadirs. Uncertainty: medium. Sampled sensitivity ratios include restraining values of 0.79 to 0.94, showing the layer is not one-directional, and only 24 of 6214 device statuses were supplied so the sensitivity values are a sample rather than a distribution; GLP-1 dosing on 2026-08-14, 08-17, and 08-20 may also have shifted true sensitivity mid-window. Dependencies: must be tested separately from the SMB interval change and after the max_iob guard, because all three act on the same overshoot evidence. All five components have values, so verify does not apply.

Evidence: both parameters govern COB decay and meal absorption modelling, and COB was reported as 0 in all 24 sampled loop statuses with carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0, extended_carb_entries 0, and average_extended_carb_duration_min null, so neither value influenced a single dosing decision in the period. Uncertainty: this is a keep because change is unsupported, not because the values are validated; no evidence exists in either direction, and no absorption duration is inferred from any aggregate. Dependencies: if carbohydrate logging begins as proposed, these two values, min_carbs_required_grams, the COB-related activation switches, and the carb ratio segments all become live at once, which is precisely the simultaneous dependent change the workflow forbids; they should therefore be reviewed only after several announced meals exist. Both components have values, so verify does not apply.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Treat the current setup as UAM-only meal coverage with retrospective micro-corrections, and make carbohydrate announcement itself the first meal-strategy step before adjusting prebolus timing, any immediate bolus percentage, or e-carbs. Concretely: keep SMB and UAM enabled, since with COB permanently zero they are the only meal coverage present and aggregate control remains good; do not set a prebolus interval or an immediate bolus percentage yet, because no carbohydrate entry exists to time or split a dose against, and the package contains no declared prebolus_minutes or immediate_bolus_percent value; and leave e-carbs unused for now, because the observed 4 to 6 hour tails have several unresolved alternative explanations. Instead, log carbohydrate grams and timestamps for the morning meal only, plus every rescue carbohydrate at any hour, so that COB, carb ratio, and the absorption model begin receiving real input. Once at least one recurring meal is announced, prebolus timing and any split percentage can be discussed against measured post-meal curves rather than inferred ones. Throughout, any change that increases meal-time insulin must avoid the afternoon, because afternoon insulin under a 10-hour DIA is what feeds the 18:00 to 19:00 local hypoglycemia cluster.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The dominant pattern is that meals are entirely unannounced: zero carbohydrate entries, zero grams, no extended carbohydrates, and COB reported as 0 in all sampled loop statuses across 14 days, while three recurring rises are clearly visible at 08:00 to 10:00, 11:00 to 17:00, and 20:00 to 23:00 local. Corrections are placed into already-rising glucose, and 17 of 24 response windows involve doses of 0.25 units or less. Four windows show a nadir followed within 60 to 120 minutes by a rise too large for basal withdrawal alone, including 47 to 204 mg/dL on 2026-08-13 and 71 to 225 mg/dL on 2026-08-12, consistent with unlogged rescue carbohydrate. The meal problem is therefore an information problem rather than a dosing-parameter problem, and every downstream meal parameter is untestable for the same single reason. The user-declared analysis_context is present with source declared_by_user but contains an empty meal_strategies array and a null strategy_stable_for_period, so declared strategy and observed telemetry agree that no meal-bolus workflow is in use; this agreement is noted rather than treated as confirmation of any specific value. Confidence in the description of observed execution is high, while confidence in any meal-parameter conclusion is low, so the overall rating is set to low.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log carbohydrate grams and timestamps for the morning meal at 08:00 to 10:00 local, and for every rescue carbohydrate at any hour, for 10 consecutive days while changing nothing else. This single observation unblocks carb ratio validation, gives COB and the absorption model real input, converts the suspected rescue-carbohydrate rebounds into data, and allows the 23:00 to 03:00 lows to be stratified against evening intake.

exceptions.suggestion: If carbohydrate logging is introduced anywhere first, introduce it here.
exceptions.rationale: This window shows a consistent rise from 110.5 to 132.9 to 148.0 mg/dL with 20.2 percent time above range by 10:00, yet time below range is 0.0 percent at 08:00 and 09:00 and only 1.2 percent at 10:00, the lowest hypoglycemia exposure of any meal window. The underlying basal is already corroborated by 95 to 99 percent time in range from 04:00 to 07:00 local, so the effect of announcing carbohydrate can be isolated here with the least downside risk.

exceptions.suggestion: Do not add meal-time insulin aggressiveness in this window during early testing; observe it unchanged instead.
exceptions.rationale: This window rises to maxima of 204, 234, and 249 mg/dL and is immediately followed by the overnight hypoglycemia cluster with time below range of 10.1 percent at 23:00, 11.4 percent at 00:00, 18.5 percent at 01:00, and about 10.2 percent at 02:00 and 03:00 local. The final status in the package, at 22:09 local on 2026-08-21, shows this window at its worst with 245.7 mg/dL, 5.935 units of insulin on board, an effective target of 80 mg/dL and sensitivity of 27.8, and no follow-up CGM data. Insulin added at this meal is the most likely to convert directly into overnight hypoglycemia through the 10-hour DIA tail.

implementation_steps: Step 0, before any change: share this analysis with the diabetes care team and agree which items, if any, are appropriate. Nothing here should be applied automatically or without independent verification, and only one change should be made at a time.

Step 1, data and profile first: keep all 17 profile values unchanged and start the night-stratification observation. For 10 days, record for each night whether the 20:00 to 23:00 local window exceeded 200 mg/dL, then compare the 23:00 to 03:00 local curves on quiet evenings against those following excursions. This separates overnight basal or target from the evening insulin tail without changing anything.

Step 2, first automation change, guard only: discuss reducing max_iob from 25 units toward a value that still sits clearly above normal peak usage, for example 8 to 10 units given the observed maximum of 5.935 units and an estimated 16 to 20 units per day. Change nothing else. Observe for 10 days whether any loop status reports the limit being reached during normal meals, and whether time below range at 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 03:00 local falls.

Step 3, second automation change, only after step 2 has been observed: discuss reducing the dynamic ISF adjustment factor from 70 percent toward 55 to 60 percent. Do not change the SMB interval in the same cycle. Observe for 10 days the effective sensitivity values reported above 200 mg/dL and the size of post-correction drops at 120 minutes, and confirm the afternoon plateau has not worsened materially.

Step 4, third automation change, only if steps 2 and 3 left the evening lows unresolved: discuss increasing the SMB interval from 3 minutes toward 5 to 8 minutes to match the CGM cadence. Note that the declared SMB minute caps do not appear to bound delivered SMB size in this build, so the interval is the more reliable lever in that group. Observe peak daily insulin on board and afternoon time above range for 10 days.

Step 5, meal strategy, run in parallel only as an observation and never combined with an insulin-delivery change in the same cycle: log carbohydrate grams and timestamps for the morning meal at 08:00 to 10:00 local and for every rescue carbohydrate at any hour, for 10 consecutive days. Confirm that COB becomes non-zero in loop statuses.

Step 6, after several announced meals exist: revisit the 08:00 carb ratio of 13.2 g per unit, then prebolus timing, then any immediate bolus percentage, one at a time and in that order. Do not introduce e-carbs at this stage; e-carbs declare carbohydrate arriving over time and are not the same as a pump extended bolus, and adding COB, an absorption profile, and a start offset together would be three simultaneous dependent changes.

Step 7, only after the above are settled: reconsider DIA of 10 hours, the flat ISF anchor of 56 mg/dL per unit, and the overnight targets, in that order and one at a time. Each of these alters insulin-on-board accounting or correction strength across every other setting, so none should be touched while the earlier steps are still being evaluated.

Throughout: exclude 2026-08-14 as the GLP-1 initiation day, 2026-08-19 for the documented occlusion and pump error, and 2026-08-21 for the sensor change from any before-and-after comparison, and repeat any observation that lands on a site change, sensor change, or GLP-1 dosing day.
education: Time below range is usually assessed against roughly 4 percent overall and 1 percent below 54 mg/dL. This dataset shows 5.1 percent overall with three level-2 readings, and the value is concentrated in two clock windows rather than spread evenly, which is generally a more informative signal than the daily average alone.

A coefficient of variation at or below about 36 percent is a common stability marker. At 32.6 percent, day-to-day variability here is within that marker, which is why the analysis focuses on specific time windows rather than on overall instability.

When dynamic sensitivity is enabled, the profile ISF acts as an anchor that the algorithm scales rather than as the sensitivity actually used. Effective sensitivity in this period ranged from about 124 to about 28 mg/dL per unit around an anchor of 56, so reviewing the scaling factor and reviewing the profile ISF are two different questions.

A sensitivity ratio of 1 in loop output means the current adjustment is neutral. It does not indicate that autosens is switched off, and it should not be read as evidence about the autosens setting itself.
The remaining-time text that appears in SMB reason strings describes how long a waiting condition still has to run. It is not the configured SMB interval and should not be used to infer that setting.
UAM estimates insulin need from unexplained glucose rises. When carbohydrate is also entered, the algorithm accounts for both; UAM does not automatically double-count announced carbohydrate.

A long DIA flattens the modelled insulin decay curve, which keeps insulin nominally active for longer and makes insulin-on-board accumulation more likely when microboluses are frequent. This is why DIA, SMB interval, and any insulin-on-board limit interact and are best reviewed one at a time.

Extended carbohydrates and a pump extended bolus are different tools. Extended carbohydrates tell the algorithm that carbohydrate will arrive over a period so it can build carbohydrate-on-board and predict accordingly, whereas an extended bolus delivers insulin over a period. Neither appears anywhere in this dataset.

A maximum insulin-on-board limit set far above realistic daily use behaves as no limit at all. Its purpose is to cap worst-case accumulation, not to shape routine dosing, which is why it can often be reviewed independently of dose-calculating settings.

When a high temporary target is active and the setting for microboluses under high temporary targets is off, microboluses are suppressed even if microboluses are otherwise always enabled. Long high temporary targets therefore change how the following hours should be interpreted.

Rises that follow a low are common and can reflect rescue carbohydrate, the body's own counter-regulation, or both. If rescue carbohydrate is not recorded, both the true depth of the low and the true carbohydrate load of the day are under-represented in the data.

Sensor warm-up periods, infusion site changes, occlusions, and newly started medications such as GLP-1 receptor agonists can all shift glucose patterns independently of pump settings, so days containing these events are usually set aside when judging whether a setting change worked.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. It is not medical advice, and it does not replace the judgement of the diabetes care team. Every proposed change must be independently verified before it is considered.
Nothing here should be applied automatically to AAPS. Any change must be entered deliberately by the user after discussion with the care team.

Make only one change at a time and allow enough observation time before judging the result. Several settings in this package explain the same patterns, and changing them together would make the outcome impossible to interpret.

The highest-priority safety finding is hypoglycemia at 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 03:00 local, including readings of 41 and 42 mg/dL. Any discussion that would increase insulin exposure in the afternoon or evening should be treated with particular caution because of the 10-hour DIA tail.

The final record in the package, at 22:09 local on 2026-08-21, shows 245.7 mg/dL with 5.935 units of insulin on board, an effective target of 80 mg/dL, and a 4 U/h rate, with no subsequent CGM data available. The outcome of that episode is unknown from this data and warrants review, keeping in mind that a sensor change earlier that day is an alternative explanation for the trace.

Occlusion and pump-error announcements were recorded on 2026-08-19, and site changes on 2026-08-10, 2026-08-13, and 2026-08-17. Unexplained highs should always prompt a check of the infusion site and pump function before any setting is adjusted.

GLP-1 doses on 2026-08-14, 2026-08-17, and 2026-08-20 fall inside the analysis window and may have altered insulin sensitivity and gastric emptying mid-period. Any changes to insulin settings while this medication is being established should be discussed with the prescribing clinician.

Hypoglycemia treatment should follow the plan already agreed with the care team, and rescue carbohydrate should be available at all times, particularly during the identified evening and overnight windows.
Recording rescue carbohydrate is a safety measure as well as a data measure, because unlogged treatment hides the true depth and frequency of low glucose from both the algorithm and any later review.

Loop behavior in this dataset includes effective targets between 80 and 116 mg/dL that do not match the declared 90 and 100 mg/dL schedule, and delivered microbolus sizes larger than the declared settings imply. Before changing any setting, confirm with the care team which build and configuration are actually running, since the declared values may not fully describe live behavior.
Increase monitoring frequency after any change, especially overnight and in the late afternoon, and revert to the previous setting and seek clinical advice if severe or unusual hypoglycemia occurs.
